summary: Make adjustments to align with server capabilities

summary: Normal processing when no adjustments needed

summary: Support empty and id-only payload types

summary: Document implementation details

summary: Client review of server documentation

summary: Patient-facing app servers must support specific SMART scope for vital signs creation
text: "Servers providing the ability to write FHIR vital sign Observation resources from patient-facing apps SHALL support the registration and authorization of apps with the patient/Observation.c?category=http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/observation-category vital-signs SMART scope or a broader version of this scope such as patient/Observation.c."
context: Patient-facing applications require specific SMART scopes to write vital sign observations, with granular permission control based on observation categories.

summary: Patient-facing app servers should support SMART scope for vital signs updates

context: Patient-facing applications should have the ability to update previously submitted vital sign observations through appropriate SMART scopes.

summary: Servers must omit unsupported scopes from access tokens
text: "If patients and apps attempting to write data are not enabled, and this can be discerned during the authorization process, the Server SHALL omit these unsupported scopes from the resulting access token."
context: When servers can determine during authorization that patients or apps are not enabled for data writing, they must exclude the relevant scopes from issued access tokens.

summary: Servers must return error for unauthorized observation submissions
text: "If an app uses an access token without the required scopes to submit an Observation or the patient is not enabled to write data, the Server SHALL return an error and SHOULD include an OperationOutcome in the response body."
context: Servers must enforce access control by rejecting observation submissions from apps lacking proper authorization or when patients are not enabled for data writing.

summary: Provider-facing app servers must support specific SMART scopes for vital signs creation
text: "Servers providing the ability to write FHIR vital sign Observation resources from provider-facing apps SHALL support the registration and authorization of apps with the user/Observation.c?category=http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/observation-category vital-signs and system/Observation.c?category=http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/observation-category vital-signs SMART scopes or broader versions of these scopes such as user/Observation.c and system/Observation.c."
context: Provider-facing applications require both user and system level SMART scopes to create vital sign observations in clinical workflows.

summary: Provider-facing app servers should support SMART scopes for vital signs updates
text: "Servers providing the ability to write FHIR vital sign Observation resources from provider-facing apps SHOULD also support the registration and authorization of apps with either user/Observation.u?category=http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/observation-category vital-signs and system/Observation.u?category=http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/observation-category vital-signs SMART scopes, or broader versions of these scopes such as user/Observation.u and system/Observation.u."
context: Provider-facing applications should have the ability to update vital sign observations through user and system level SMART scopes.

summary: Servers must document supported scopes in SMART configuration

context: FHIR servers must publish their supported SMART scopes in a discoverable location to enable client applications to understand available permissions.

summary: Servers must support submission of non-calculated vital sign observations
text: "Servers SHALL support the submission of Observation resources that *are not* the result of a calculation and validate against a [US Core Vital Sign Profile](https://build.fhir.org/ig/HL7/US-Core/profiles-and-extensions.html#observation) that corresponds to a version used by the Server for vital sign Observation read requests."
context: FHIR servers must accept direct vital sign measurements (non-calculated values) that conform to US Core vital sign profiles consistent with their read capabilities.

summary: Servers may support submission of calculated vital sign observations
text: "Servers MAY support the submission of Observation resources that *are* the result of a calculation (such as the \"US Core Pediatric BMI for Age Observation Profile\") and validate against a [US Core Vital Sign Profile](https://build.fhir.org/ig/HL7/US-Core/profiles-and-extensions.html#observation) that corresponds to a version used by the Server for vital sign Observation read requests."
context: FHIR servers have the option to accept calculated vital sign values like BMI that derive from other measurements.

summary: Servers must respond appropriately to valid vital sign creation requests
text: "Servers SHALL respond to supported and valid vital sign Observation creation requests with a status code of 200 OK and a content location header, or with a status code of 202 Accepted."
context: FHIR servers must provide standardized HTTP responses to successful vital sign observation creation requests.

summary: Resources must be visible after creation when content location header provided
text: "If a content location header is provided, the resources SHALL be visible in subsequent read API calls and accessible within the system in the same manner as other patient-submitted data."
context: When servers provide a content location header in creation responses, they commit to making the resource immediately available through standard read operations.

summary: Servers must document reason for discarding resources when no content location provided
text: "If a content location header is not provided, and the Server does not subsequently make the resource accessible in read API calls, the Server SHALL have a documented and discoverable reason why it was discarded (e.g., a log entry describing rejection during a review workflow or the applicability of a condition in the \"Discarding\" section below)."
context: When servers accept resources but don't make them immediately available, they must provide traceable documentation of the disposition decision.

summary: Servers must support single vital sign creation
text: "Servers SHALL support the creation of a single vital sign through a FHIR create operation, and MAY support the creation of multiple vital signs by submitting a FHIR Batch bundle."

summary: Provider-facing apps must include patient-supplied tag for patient-mediated data

context: Provider-facing applications must properly tag observations that originate from patients to distinguish them from provider-generated data.

summary: Servers must associate patient-supplied tag with patient-written vital signs

context: FHIR servers must maintain provenance information by tagging patient-supplied data appropriately.

summary: Provider-facing apps must include patient-supplied tag when writing patient data
text: "Provider-facing apps writing data supplied by a patient SHALL include this tag in the submitted Observation resources."
context: Provider-facing applications have a responsibility to properly identify the source of patient-supplied data when submitting observations.

summary: Client apps must use server encounter reference when populating encounter element
text: "If populating this element, apps SHALL use a reference to an Encounter resource in the Server, and MAY use the value returned by the launch/encounter SMART scope."
context: When client applications associate observations with encounters, they must reference existing server resources to maintain referential integrity.

summary: Servers should document encounter element requirements
text: "Systems SHOULD document whether the encounter element is required to create a vital sign."
context: Servers should provide clear guidance to client applications about when encounter references are mandatory for observation creation.

summary: Apps must populate subject reference with Patient resource
text: "Apps SHALL populate the subject reference with a reference to a Patient resource in the Server."
context: All observation submissions must be properly associated with a patient resource in the target server.

summary: Patient-facing apps should use SMART launch context for subject reference
text: "Patient-facing apps SHOULD populate this element based on the value returned as part of the launch/patient SMART scope."
context: Patient-facing applications should leverage SMART launch context to automatically associate observations with the correct patient.

summary: Contained device resources must populate deviceName element
text: "Contained device resources SHALL populate at least one deviceName element."
context: When client applications include device information as contained resources, they must provide identifying information about the device.

summary: Servers must return device reference in subsequent reads
text: "When this value is populated with a reference to a Device resource on the Server, Servers SHALL return this reference in subsequent reads operations of the resource that was created."
context: Servers must maintain referential integrity for device references in stored observations.

summary: Servers must not return error for valid contained Device resource
text: "Servers SHALL not return an error due to the presence of a valid contained Device resource."
context: FHIR servers must accept observations with properly formatted contained device resources without generating errors.

summary: Servers should document behavior with contained Device resources
text: "Servers SHOULD document their behavior with regard to contained Device resources."
context: Servers should provide clear documentation about how they handle contained device resources to set proper client expectations.

summary: Patient-facing apps must set performer to patient for patient-collected data
text: "For patient-facing apps, if the app knows that a patient collected this data, the app SHALL set the performer to a reference to the patient based on the SMART launch context (this should also match the Observation.subject)."
context: Patient-facing applications must accurately identify when patients themselves performed the vital sign measurement.

summary: Apps should populate performer display when resource cannot be created
text: "If the relevant resource does not exist and the app cannot create it, the app SHOULD populate performer.display."
context: When client applications cannot establish proper resource references for performers, they should provide human-readable identification.

summary: Servers must return performer value in subsequent reads
text: "When this value is populated in a successful create operation, systems SHALL return it in subsequent read operations of the resource that was created."
context: Servers must preserve performer information provided during observation creation for future retrievals.

summary: Servers must document observation discarding behavior
text: "Systems SHALL clearly document this behavior or the ways in which health systems may customize this behavior in the API documentation."
context: When servers discard observations due to temporal proximity or other factors, they must provide transparent documentation of these policies.

summary: Servers must document duplicate observation handling behavior
text: "Systems SHALL clearly document this behavior or the ways in which health systems may customize this behavior in the API documentation."
context: When servers detect and handle duplicate observations, they must provide clear documentation of their duplicate detection and handling policies.

summary: Servers should support patient apps updating observation status to entered-in-error

context: Patient-facing applications should be able to correct data submission mistakes by marking observations as entered-in-error.

summary: Servers must not return error for contained Provenance resources

context: FHIR servers must accept observations with contained provenance information without generating errors, even if they don't process the provenance data.

summary: Apps must pass through unaltered Provenance resources from external sources
text: "Apps SHALL pass through any Provenance resources received from the source system, unaltered (except for references, as described below), as contained resources on the Observation."
context: When transferring observations from external systems, client applications must preserve original provenance information to maintain data lineage.

summary: Apps must pass through referenced Must Support resources

summary: Apps must generate Provenance resource when author not received from source

context: Client applications must create appropriate provenance records when original authorship information is not available from source systems.

summary: Extension URL must be fixed value for interpreter needed extension
